topicName: Authentication Integrations (LDAP, SAML, OIDC, Active Directory)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Authentication Integrations in Jenkins (LDAP, SAML, OIDC, Active Directory)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Enterprise environments require centralized user authentication and authorization. Jenkins supports multiple authentication protocols including LDAP, Active Directory, SAML, and OpenID Connect (OIDC). This tutorial covers configuring these integrations for secure access control."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Administrator access to your Jenkins instance."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Required security plugins installed (e.g., LDAP Plugin, Active Directory Plugin, SAML Plugin, or OpenID Connect Authentication Plugin)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Valid credentials and endpoints from your Identity Provider (IdP)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Integrating LDAP and Active Directory"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To configure LDAP or Active Directory, navigate to Manage Jenkins > Security > Configure Global Security. Set the Security Realm to LDAP or Active Directory."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"Server: ldap://dc01.corp.example.com:389
Root DN: dc=corp,-example,dc=com
User Search Base: cn=Users
User Search Filter: sAMAccountName={0}
Manager DN: cn=jenkins-service,cn=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com
Manager Password: secure_password"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Integrating SAML (Single Sign-On)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"For modern IdPs like Okta, Azure AD, or Keycloak, SAML 2.0 provides seamless Single Sign-On. Install the SAML Plugin and configure the IdP metadata."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"IDP Metadata: https://identity.example.com/idp/metadata.xml
Entity ID: https://jenkins.example.com/securityRealm/finishLogin
Display Name Attribute: http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/name
Group Attribute: http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Integrating OIDC (OpenID Connect)"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"OpenID Connect utilizes JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for authentication. Install the OpenID Connect Authentication Plugin and provide the discovery endpoint."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"Client ID: jenkins-auth-client
Client Secret: [STORED_IN_JENKINS_CREDENTIALS]
Well-known Configuration URL: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
User Name Field: preferred_username"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Authorization Strategy Configuration"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once authentication is established, configure the Authorization strategy to determine what authenticated users can do. Matrix-based security or Role-Based Strategy plugins are recommended for fine-grained access control."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Role-Based Strategy: Assign permissions based on user groups mapped from LDAP, SAML, or OIDC claims."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Matrix-based Security: Explicitly define permissions per user or group."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Validation and Troubleshooting"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always keep a local admin user enabled (using the Matrix strategy override if supported) before saving authentication changes to prevent lockout. Use Jenkins system logs under java.util.logging or specific plugin loggers to debug binding and token exchange issues."}]
